Logarithms

A logarithm answers the question "what power?": log⁡bx is the exponent you put on the base b to get x. This calculator evaluates logarithms in any valid base — exactly when the answer is a fraction such as log⁡48=32 — and solves two common equation types: logarithmic equations log⁡b(ax+c)=d and exponential equations bax+c=k.

Try changing the input

Evaluate log⁡2x for x=2,4,8,16: each doubling of x adds exactly 1 to the logarithm. Logarithms turn multiplication into addition.

Formulas and rules

log⁡bx=y  ⟺  by=xlog⁡bx=ln⁡xln⁡b
log⁡b(MN)=log⁡bM+log⁡bNlog⁡bMN=log⁡bM−log⁡bNlog⁡b(Mk)=klog⁡bM
SymbolMeaning
bBase: positive and not equal to 1. Base 10 is the common log; base e≈2.71828 is the natural log ln⁡.
xArgument: must be positive.

Worked example

Solve 5x−1=200

Step 1 — Take log⁡5 of both sides

x−1=log⁡5200

Step 2 — Change of base

log⁡5200=ln⁡200ln⁡5≈5.2983171.609438≈3.292030

Step 3 — Solve

x≈3.292030+1=4.292030

Assumptions, domain and rounding

  • Only real logarithms are used: the base must be positive and not 1, and every logarithm's argument must be positive.
  • An exponential equation bax+c=k has a solution only when k>0.
  • Supported equation types are exactly the two listed above; other forms (such as sums of logarithms) are not solved here.
  • Type e as the base for natural logarithms. Results are rounded to 6 decimal places unless exact.
